Everett Wess

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, Alabama · Open seat

Attorney; managing partner, The Wess Law Firm, P.C. (Birmingham)

Everett Wess is a Birmingham attorney who has been a municipal judge, a city prosecutor and a public defender, and before law school he worked as a software engineer on NASA contracts in Huntsville. He ran in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, then beat Dakarai Larriett in the June 16 runoff with about 54.7% of the vote. He faces Republican U.S. Rep. Barry Moore on November 3, 2026, for the seat Sen. Tommy Tuberville is leaving to run for governor.

Where Wess stands

Cost of living / affordability
Says rising grocery and gas prices are hurting Alabama families. Argues Congress should put the needs of Alabama consumers first and links affordability to U.S. involvement in overseas conflicts.
Foreign policy / war powers
Says the United States should get out of its current war. Says pursuing congressional action on war powers would be one of his priorities.
Healthcare
Calls healthcare access, especially in rural areas, one of Alabama's biggest issues. Proposes looking at combining rural and veterans' healthcare services and says healthcare is "a need, it's not a want."
Rural hospitals
Questions whether federal rural healthcare funding will help communities without hospitals over the long term. Says he is concerned facilities and staff may not remain once the funding ends.
Infrastructure
Says Alabama should use federal funding for transportation, broadband and other projects. Says infrastructure is an area where he would put the state's interests first.
Minimum wage
Campaigned on raising the federal minimum wage.
Public safety
Campaigned on building safe communities. Lists public safety as one of his focus issues along with the economy and healthcare.

Background

  • Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Alabama (won June 16, 2026 runoff)
  • Managing partner, The Wess Law Firm, P.C. (2000–present)
  • Municipal Court judge, City of Midfield, Jefferson County
  • Former prosecutor, City of Midfield; former public defender, City of Irondale
  • Former adjunct professor, Faulkner University
  • About 17 years in IT, mostly as a software engineer in Huntsville, including on NASA contracts (TRW, NTI Corp., Comsys, Banctec)
  • A.A., music education, Selma University; B.S., computer science, and MBA, Alabama A&M University; J.D., Birmingham School of Law
